name: Electromagnetic induction (Faraday, Lenz, eddy currents, self and mutual inductance)
RMS value of non-sinusoidal waveforms
description: Calculation of root mean square value for non-sinusoidal currents and periodic waveforms. Excludes standard sinusoidal AC RMS calculations.
example_stems: The electric current in a circuit is given by i = i0(t/T). The r.m.s. current for the period from t=0 to t=T is ____. | Calculate the rms value for a triangular current wave of peak value i0.

name: Inductive reactance and inductor energy
description: Inductive reactance XL = omega L, magnetic energy stored in an inductor 1/2 L I^2, and power dissipation in resistive inductors. Excludes capacitive circuits.
example_stems: An inductor stores 16 J of magnetic-field energy and dissipates 32 W of thermal energy when a.c. current of 2 A flows through it. Find XL/R. | An alternating voltage is applied across a pure inductor of 0.05 H. Find inductive reactance at 50 Hz.

name: Capacitive reactance
description: Capacitive reactance XC = 1/(omega C) and capacitor response in AC circuits. Excludes inductive circuits.
example_stems: Find the capacitive reactance of a 10 microfarad capacitor connected to a 220 V, 50 Hz source. | A capacitor blocks DC and offers reactance to AC; calculate reactance at 1 kHz.

name: Impedance and phase angle
description: Impedance Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL-XC)^2) and phase angle phi in series LCR circuits. Excludes resonant condition and LC oscillations.
example_stems: For the series LCR circuit connected with a 220 V source, XL=70, XC=150 and R=60. The power factor is alpha/10. Find alpha. | Calculate the phase angle between voltage and current in an LCR circuit with given component values.

name: LC oscillations (energy exchange)
description: LC oscillations, energy exchange between electric field of capacitor and magnetic field of inductor, oscillation frequency omega = 1/sqrt(LC). Excludes external damping or driving source.
example_stems: A capacitor C is first charged fully with potential difference V0 and connected across inductor L. In t s, 25% energy is transferred to inductor. Find t. | In an LC circuit, energy oscillates sinusoidally between capacitor and inductor; find the oscillation period.

name: Resonance condition and maximum current
description: Series resonance condition omega L = 1/(omega C), resonant frequency, impedance minimum, and maximum current at resonance. Excludes off-resonance power factor.
example_stems: Using a variable-frequency a.c. voltage source, the maximum current measured in the given LCR circuit is 50 mA for V=5 sin(100t). Find C. | At series resonance in an LCR circuit, find the resonance frequency and maximum current.

name: Power in AC circuits and wattless current
Power factor
description: Average power in AC circuits P = Vrms Irms cos phi and power factor cos phi = R/Z. Excludes purely reactive wattless current.
example_stems: An AC circuit has impedance 100 ohm and resistance 60 ohm; find the power factor. | A circuit draws 5 A at 220 V with power factor 0.8; find the true power consumed.

name: Wattless current
description: Wattless current Irms sin phi in purely reactive or low power factor AC circuits. Excludes active (wattful) power dissipation.
example_stems: A current of 5 A flows in an AC circuit with a phase lag of 60 degrees. Find the wattless component of current. | Show that in a purely inductive circuit the average power dissipated is zero and current is wattless.
